rules.title: California Civil Code section 1950.5 (Security deposits for residential rental property)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not demand or receive security above one month's rent (two months for small natural-person landlords owning no more than two properties with four units total, except for service members). Landlords must do an initial inspection on request, photograph the unit, and return the deposit with an itemized statement within 21 days of move-out.
rules.key_value: Max 1 month's rent; 2 months for small natural-person landlords (≤2 properties, ≤4 units); return within 21 calendar days
rules.penalty: Landlord who in bad faith fails to comply with the return and itemization rules forfeits the right to claim any amount of the security.
rules.status_basis: Section of the California Civil Code; the 1-month cap applies to security collected on or after July 1, 2024.

coverage.summary: Applies to security for rental agreements of residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.

rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
